feature: Words that travel into a title are never cut off by their own box
summary: Words that rise, track or flip into a title are drawn whole the whole way in, even where they pass outside their text box. Before, a rising word was sliced flat along the bottom of its box until it landed.
setup: Photonz Next, no switch changed from its defaults, a video open (the sample recording works). Walk: Scripts/playtest/title-set-keynote-clean-walk.json.

try.do: Open the Library, pick Comps, and insert Keynote Clean at the playhead at 0:00.
Press Home, then step forward a quarter second twice.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Look at the second word rising in: its bottom is drawn below the selection box, not cut along it.
Press Space and watch the headline come in at full speed.
Export the video and scrub the first second of the title in the exported file.
Open queue/audits/2026-10-16-words-whole-contact.png and compare each Before and After row.

evaluate: Does the rising headline in Keynote Clean now look whole from its first frame?
Does a word drawn briefly outside its selection box while it travels bother you?
In the Track In row, do the outer letters coming from past the line's ends look right?
Does the exported file match what you saw on the canvas?
rough: No mock covers how a travelling word meets its text box; this follows the depth flips, which already drew past it.
Mid-move, words can sit outside the selection outline on the canvas. They land back inside it.
Mask Reveal's first sliver now shows in the mask's own thin margin under the line, which the box used to cut: it starts a frame or so sooner.

Track In by letter in a tight box gives the picture a lot of room while its outer letters are far out (521 px each side on a 1080p headline); measured at 1080p with motion blur it draws in 5.6 ms a frame, the same as without the room.
